hypotheses.justification: The statement `posDetInt n ≤ (commensurator (SLnZ n)).toSubmonoid` elaborates without `NeZero n`. `SLnZ` (line 74) and `posDetInt` (line 257) are defined before the first `variable [NeZero n]` at line 460, and they only need `Fin n`. The statement is also true for `n = 0`. `GL (Fin 0) ℚ` is the unit group of `Matrix (Fin 0) (Fin 0) ℚ`, which has one element, so it is a subsingleton group. Every element is `1`, and `1` lies in the commensurator (`one_mem`). Hence the inequality holds trivially for `n = 0`. For `n ≠ 0`, the current proof still works. Use `omit [NeZero n] in`, split on `n = 0` versus `n ≠ 0`, and in the second case supply `haveI : NeZero n := ⟨hn⟩` before applying `mem_commensurator_of_hasIntEntries n hg.1`. The only place `NeZero n` is really used is `conj_mat_det_one`, for `n - 1 + 1 = n` in the determinant computation. That lemma is itself only needed for `n ≠ 0`.
